title: A 60 frame a second recording edits and exports at 60 frames a second
goal: Photonz records the screen at 60 frames a second, but every video it opens is cut, timed and exported on a fixed 30 frame grid, so half of every recording's frames are thrown away and fast scrolling and pointer motion come out choppier than the recording itself. A video should keep the rate of what is in it: an edit made from 60 frame recordings is a 60 frame edit, steps one sixtieth of a second at a time, and exports at 60, while an edit of 30 frame footage stays at 30 exactly as today.
notes: Focus success line 2 says 1x plays every frame at the document rate, 60 fps where the source is. Today the rate is a constant: Sources/PhotonzCore/MovieClip.swift MovieRef.framesPerSecond = 30, frameStepMS = 33 (exactly 30 since 2026-11-22, ce69dc74b); Sources/PhotonzCore/DocumentVideoExport.swift movieFPS = 30 with a comment saying 30 is finer than any screen recording the app makes, which is not true: Sources/Photonz/Capture/ScreenRecorder.swift:332 records at fps = 60, and Sources/PhotonzCore/ReferenceEdit.swift framesPerSecond = 60. Users of the constant: TimelineTrack, DocumentVideoExport, VideoTimecode, KeyLanesView, ReferenceFootage, FreezeLength, ClipNudge, ClipFilmstrip, DocumentTime, AgentContactSheet, ClosingRecording. Reproduction 2026-11-24 manager pass: a walk at /tmp/mgr-fps/walk.json with setup referenceEdit 6 and a speed export step {seconds:5, keep:"five-seconds.mp4"} ran via Scripts/playtest.sh; ffprobe of the source: r_frame_rate=60/1 nb_frames=3600 duration=60; ffprobe of the export: width=3456 height=2234 r_frame_rate=30/1 nb_frames=150 duration=5.0. Export took 3.2 s for 5 s. Speed walk baseline short-6.json says frameStepMS 33 and plays.whole.framesDue 1817 a minute, which is 30 a second. Keep the codable change backward compatible (decodeIfPresent, default 30). The doc to update: docs/design/video.md (every place it says thirty times a second). Second half, playback at 60, is its own task that waits on this one.
acceptance: Reproduced first and pasted into the audit: 5 seconds of the 6 minute reference edit (its four recordings are 60/1 by ffprobe, 3600 frames a minute) export today as 150 frames at r_frame_rate 30/1; after the fix the same 5 seconds export as 300 frames at 60/1, and no two neighbouring frames of a stretch where the recording moves are the same picture

Test first in PhotonzCore: a video document carries its own frame rate (taken from its recordings, the highest of them up to 60; a document with no recordings, or one saved before this change, reads as 30), and the frame grid (MovieRef.gridFrame / gridMS / frameStepMS and FreezeLength, VideoTimecode, ClipNudge, ClipFilmstrip, DocumentTime.shortestMS) asks the document for its rate instead of a constant. Tests cover a 30 frame edit staying frame for frame what it is today, a 60 frame edit, a mixed one, and an old file opening unchanged

Export writes at the document's rate (DocumentVideoExport.movieFPS becomes the document's rate); GIF and animated HEIC keep their own lower rates. The 6 minute reference edit still exports in no more than its own length (2026-11-16: 117.6 s at 30), number before and after in the audit
Frame stepping (arrow keys, the clip nudge) and View > Timecode count in the document's frames, so a 60 frame edit steps a sixtieth at a time and its timecode reads 0 to 59

Ships on by default in Next behind a new flag in FeatureCatalog (suggested next-video-keeps-its-recorded-frame-rate); Current keeps 30. Try it: open the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev from the audit's button, export 5 seconds and read the file's rate in Finder's Get Info, then press the right arrow and watch the timecode step one frame

Speed walk short form and the video walks stay green at Next defaults (Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh, Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build export, an-editing-session-walk); playback itself may still step at 30 until the follow-up task makes it play at 60, and the audit says which it does
Audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
